I can reproduce this using GodotPhysics3D too, the effect is less noticeable but it's there.

As far as I can see the order of operations is as follows, first the animation set the position:

```
Node3D::set_position(const Vector3 & p_position) Line 707
call_with_variant_args_helper<Node3D,Vector3 const &,0>(Node3D * p_instance, void(Node3D::*)(const Vector3 &) p_method, const Variant * * p_args, Callable::CallError & r_error, IndexSequence<0> __formal) Line 224
call_with_variant_args_dv<Node3D,Vector3 const &>(Node3D * p_instance, void(Node3D::*)(const Vector3 &) p_method, const Variant * * p_args, int p_argcount, Callable::CallError & r_error, const Vector<Variant> & default_values) Line 371
MethodBindT<Node3D,Vector3 const &>::call(Object * p_object, const Variant * * p_args, int p_arg_count, Callable::CallError & r_error) Line 339
ClassDB::set_property(Object * p_object, const StringName & p_property, const Variant & p_value, bool * r_valid) Line 1677
Object::set(const StringName & p_name, const Variant & p_value, bool * r_valid) Line 361
Object::set_indexed(const Vector<StringName> & p_names, const Variant & p_value, bool * r_valid) Line 502
AnimationMixer::_blend_apply() Line 1955
AnimationMixer::_process_animation(double p_delta, bool p_update_only) Line 1009
AnimationMixer::_notification(int p_what) Line 2365
AnimationMixer::_notification_forwardv(int p_notification) Line 43
AnimationPlayer::_notification_forwardv(int p_notification) Line 37
Object::_notification_forward(int p_notification) Line 1013
Object::notification(int p_notification, bool p_reversed) Line 930
SceneTree::_process_group(SceneTree::ProcessGroup * p_group, bool p_physics) Line 1194
SceneTree::_process(bool p_physics) Line 1281
SceneTree::physics_process(double p_time) Line 646
Main::iteration() Line 4849
OS_Windows::run() Line 2354
```

Then the physics server gets notified of the updated transform:

```
JoltBody3D::set_transform(Transform3D p_transform) Line 563
JoltBody3D::set_state(PhysicsServer3D::BodyState p_state, const Variant & p_value) Line 597
JoltPhysicsServer3D::body_set_state(RID p_body, PhysicsServer3D::BodyState p_state, const Variant & p_value) Line 756
PhysicsServer3DWrapMT::body_set_state(RID p1, PhysicsServer3D::BodyState p2, const Variant & p3) Line 225
CollisionObject3D::_notification(int p_what) Line 99
CollisionObject3D::_notification_forwardv(int p_notification) Line 38
PhysicsBody3D::_notification_forwardv(int p_notification) Line 39
RigidBody3D::_notification_forwardv(int p_notification) Line 37
Object::_notification_forward(int p_notification) Line 1013
Object::notification(int p_notification, bool p_reversed) Line 930
SceneTree::flush_transform_notifications() Line 202
SceneTree::physics_process(double p_time) Line 655
Main::iteration() Line 4849
OS_Windows::run() Line 2354
```

Since this is a kinematic body and because of #109885 this means that only a target position is set. Asking for the transform of the rigid body will return the old position until the physics server has stepped.

Now the camera is updated (with the old transform):

```
Camera3D::_update_camera() Line 152
Camera3D::_request_camera_update() Line 41
Camera3D::_notification(int p_what) Line 209
Camera3D::_notification_forwardv(int p_notification) Line 41
Object::_notification_forward(int p_notification) Line 1013
Object::notification(int p_notification, bool p_reversed) Line 930
SceneTree::flush_transform_notifications() Line 202
SceneTree::physics_process(double p_time) Line 655
Main::iteration() Line 4849
OS_Windows::run() Line 2354
```

Physics server is stepped:

```
JPH::PhysicsSystem::Update(float inDeltaTime, int inCollisionSteps, JPH::TempAllocator * inTempAllocator, JPH::JobSystem * inJobSystem) Line 138
JoltSpace3D::step(float p_step) Line 190
JoltPhysicsServer3D::step(float p_step) Line 1629
PhysicsServer3DWrapMT::step(float p_step) Line 62
Main::iteration() Line 4888
OS_Windows::run() Line 2354
```

and as far as I can see, the camera isn't updated anymore afterwards. This results in the camera lagging behind and since the object is both rotating and translating you experience this as jittering.

> and as far as I can see, the camera isn't updated anymore afterwards. This results in the camera lagging behind and since the object is both rotating and translating you experience this as jittering.

This is visible if camera is stationary, too. So, the real issue is https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109885 and it has to be fixed to fix this?

It is definitively a problem, but I'm not sure if it is the only problem. The current PRs that attempt to fix that issue do not solve the problem, but that is because they do not update the global transform of the body immediately (they do not flag it updated until the physics step). I need to spend more time debugging this.
If that helps, this issue is also present on CharacterBody3D and AnimatableBody3D even if they are moved during physics step.

I looked into this one again and I can no longer reproduce the issue with the 'master' version of godot. If I revert #115327 I can reproduce the issue, so it appears that it was caused by the same thing. @patrykkalinowski can you please confirm?
@jrouwe I checked minimal reproduction project on 4.7dev1 and indeed, seems to be fixed. Thanks a lot!
